 Primark brings own-label skincare to Click & Collect across 73 UK stores 
 Catherine Rowe-Kosary 20 November 2026 
 Twitter 
 Facebook 
 Linkedin 
 WhatsApp 
 Primark has made three of its own-label skincare ranges available through Click & Collect at 73 UK stores on a limited-time basis, while stocks last. 
 The offer launched on 19 November and covers PS… Glass Skin, PS… PDRN and the new PS… Glow collection. Customers can browse and order products on Primark.com before collecting them from a participating store.
 The products include cleansers, toners, serums, moisturisers and masks, with prices ranging from £1.50 to £5. Glow starts at £1.50, PDRN at £2 and Glass Skin at £4.50. Primark is marketing the selection as a K-beauty edit.
 Julie Thomsett, Head of Buying, Beauty at Primark, said: “Our customers love K-Beauty, and they love being able to get their hands on it quickly even more. Bringing Beauty to Click & Collect means customers can pick out their whole routine online and collect it from their local store, just in time for Christmas gifting and party season prep.”
 The 73-store figure applies specifically to the skincare offer, rather than Primark’s wider Click & Collect service. The retailer first trialled Click & Collect at 25 stores in north-west England, Yorkshire and north Wales, initially offering children’s clothing, nursery products and toys. The service allowed customers at smaller branches to order products that were usually only stocked in larger stores.
 Primark completed its Click & Collect rollout across Great Britain in May 2025. When it launched its UK app in April 2026, it said the wider service was live in all 189 of its stores across England, Scotland and Wales.
 The app also includes features designed to help customers plan store visits, including real-time stock checks and a store locator. At its launch, Primark said a quarter of UK visitors to its website already used its stock checker.
 The PS… ranges are separate from Pureseoul’s K-Beauty Mini Mart at Primark , which launched in September. The seven-brand edit features third-party Korean skincare and make-up, including lower-priced sister lines from established brands. Developed exclusively for Primark, it was designed for high-volume distribution at the retailer’s price points and is not sold through Pureseoul’s own stores.
